source.check: Londonderry Sentinel 2 November 1946 p5, read in the page image: 'The results of the contests in six electoral divisions were announced yesterday, and the new Council will consist of' ... 'Con Askin, Faughanvale'; News-Letter 2 November 1946 p5: 'the six contests which took place'.

note: Triennial election of Limavady rural district (23 divisions); Co. Londonderry polled 31 October 1946. Seven divisions were contested; six new members and ten retiring councillors were returned unopposed (Londonderry Sentinel, 19 October 1946, p. 6). The Sentinel of 2 November 1946, p. 5, prints the results and the full new council of 23 names, without divisions; the Nationalists won control for the first time. Seven of the retiring members' divisions are taken from the 1939 return, as each contest note says. Faughanvale added and the six unopposed new members re-cited (meetings gap-fill, 7 Nov 2026). Two nominations, Con Askin (old) and Robert J. Townley (new) (Derry Journal, 18 and 21 October 1946; Londonderry Sentinel, 19 October 1946). No poll was held in Faughanvale: the News-Letter reports 'the six contests which took place' (Ballyharrigan, Bellarena, Drumreighland, Foreglen, Gelvin, Scriggan, all recorded here), and the Sentinel's list of the new council names 'Con Askin, Faughanvale' and not Townley. Townley's withdrawal itself was not found in the reports read. Returned unopposed.
